raw: You can activate your new card in the app under Cards → Activate, either by tapping the card against your phone or by scanning it with the camera. If you want to use the card before it is activated, you can already add it to Apple Pay or Google Pay.
Chinor Bank accounts can be opened by residents aged 16 or over. To proceed, you'll need a passport or national ID card and a short selfie video to verify your identity in the app.
Chinor Bank accounts can be opened by residents aged 16 or over. To proceed, you'll need a passport or national ID card and a short selfie video to verify your identity in the app.

You can use your card at any ATM that accepts your card network. Withdrawals are free up to 2,500,000 UZS per month on Standard, and a 1.3 % fee applies above that. ATMs with no operator surcharge are marked in the app under Cards → ATMs near me.

You can use the Chinor Card Locator in the app to find the nearest ATM. Withdrawals are free up to 2,500,000 UZS per month on Standard, and a 1.3 % fee applies above that. ATMs with no operator surcharge are marked with a green dot.

You can set up Auto top-up in the app under Account → Auto top-up. Choose a balance threshold and an amount of at least 50,000 UZS; when your balance falls below the threshold, the top-up is taken from your linked card. Credit-card top-ups carry a 1.1 % fee.

Chinor does not accept cheques, so a cheque cannot be credited. Cash deposited at a Chinor ATM is credited immediately, and cash deposited at a branch counter is credited by the end of the same business day. If the deposit is still missing after that time, a human agent can check it with the deposit receipt.

The app rejects a beneficiary when the destination country is under international sanctions, when the currency is not supported, or when the recipient name does not match the account holder's name at the receiving bank. Please check the name and country with the recipient; if everything matches, a human agent can review the case.

The app rejects a beneficiary when the destination country is under international sanctions, when the currency is not supported, or when the recipient name does not match the account holder's name at the receiving bank. Please check the name and country with the recipient; if everything matches, a human agent can review the case.

If the transfer status is Scheduled, you can cancel it directly in the app. For international (SWIFT) transfers, you may request a recall within 24 hours for a 90,000 UZS fee, but this is not guaranteed as it depends on the receiving bank's agreement.

A domestic transfer can be cancelled in the app only while its status is Scheduled; once it shows Sent it cannot be cancelled. An international (SWIFT) transfer can be recalled within 24 hours of sending for a 90,000 UZS recall fee, but recall is not guaranteed.

A replacement card is sent automatically 45 days before your card expires, to the address in your profile. Your current card keeps working until the last day of its expiry month. When the new card arrives, activate it in the app under Cards → Activate.

Chinor cards work in more than 180 countries wherever the Visa or Mastercard network is accepted, except in countries under international sanctions. If a transaction is declined, the app will show the reason under the transaction.

Chinor cards work in more than 180 countries wherever the Visa or Mastercard network is accepted, except in countries under international sanctions. If a merchant declines the card, the app shows the decline reason under the transaction.

A replacement card is sent automatically 45 days before your card expires, to the address in your profile. Your current card keeps working until the last day of its expiry month. When the new card arrives, activate it in the app under Cards → Activate.

You can link a Visa, Mastercard, UzCard or Humo card issued in your own name under Account → Top up → Add card, and use it for manual or automatic top-ups. Debit-card top-ups are free; credit-card top-ups carry a 1.1 % fee.

Please check in the app that the card is activated and not frozen, and that the relevant toggle under Cards → Security is switched on. If the chip card fails at every terminal, it is treated as damaged and replaced free of charge.

Please check in the app that your card is activated and not frozen, and that the relevant toggle under Cards → Security is switched on. If the card is not working at any terminal, it will be replaced free of charge.

Freeze your card immediately in the app under Cards → Freeze, or call the 24-hour card line at +998 (71) 000-11-22. Then cancel it and order a replacement—your first replacement each calendar year is free. Dispute any unfamiliar transactions from the transaction screen within 60 days of the statement date.

If you don't recognize a payment, first check the merchant's trading name and location under the transaction in the app — it can differ from the shop name. If it still doesn't look familiar, freeze the card in the app and raise a dispute from the transaction screen (Transaction → Something wrong → Dispute) within 60 days of the statement date.

Chinor converts currency at the interbank mid-market rate, with a 0.9 % weekend markup from Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59. If you accepted to pay in your home currency, the merchant’s rate applied, and Chinor cannot refund that difference—always choose to pay in the local currency.

ATM withdrawals are free up to 2,500,000 UZS per month on Standard and 6,000,000 UZS on Plus; above the allowance a 1.3 % fee applies. Some ATM operators add their own surcharge, which the ATM shows before you confirm; Chinor does not control or refund operator surcharges.

ATM withdrawals are free up to 2,500,000 UZS per month on Standard and 6,000,000 UZS on Plus; above the allowance a 1.3 % fee applies. Some ATM operators add their own surcharge, which the ATM shows before you confirm; Chinor does not control or refund operator surcharges.

If you did not make the ATM withdrawal, freeze the card immediately, call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22, and raise a dispute from the transaction screen within 60 days of the statement date.
You can change your 4-digit PIN in the app under Cards → Security → PIN after confirming your passcode and biometrics. There is no fee, and the new PIN works from the next chip transaction.
You can change your 4-digit PIN in the app under Cards → Security → PIN after confirming your passcode and biometrics. There is no fee, and the new PIN works from the next chip transaction.

Chinor accounts are available to residents of 12 countries, and cards can be used in more than 180 countries, except those under international sanctions.

The decline reason is shown under the transaction in the app. Common causes include a frozen card, a blocked merchant category or toggle under Cards → Security, the daily limit, the merchant not completing 3-D Secure, or a fraud-monitoring check that asks you to confirm the payment in the app.

The decline reason is shown under the transaction in the app. Common causes include a frozen card, a blocked merchant category or toggle under Cards → Security, the daily limit, the merchant not completing 3-D Secure, or a fraud-monitoring check that asks you to confirm the payment in the app.

A withdrawal is usually declined because the 6,000,000 UZS daily ATM limit was reached, ATM withdrawals are switched off under Cards → Security, the PIN was wrong, the ATM does not support your card network, or the ATM is out of cash. The reason is shown under the attempt in the app.

A withdrawal is usually declined because the 6,000,000 UZS daily ATM limit was reached, ATM withdrawals are switched off under Cards → Security, the PIN was wrong, the ATM does not support your card network, or the ATM is out of cash. The reason is shown under the attempt in the app.
If your transfer failed, the app will show the reason. Declined or failed transfers are returned to your balance within 2 business days.

Virtual disposable cards can be used for online payments up to 3,000,000 UZS per day and for a single payment of up to 3,000,000 UZS. They are created instantly in the app under Cards → New virtual card and are free on both plans.

You can update your address in the app under Profile → Personal details, and the change takes effect immediately. You'll need to confirm the new address with a one-time code sent to your registered phone. If you're changing your legal name, it will be processed within 3 business days after uploading the new document.

To update your address, go to the app under Profile → Personal details. A new address is confirmed with a one-time code sent to your registered phone. If you're changing your legal name, you’ll need to upload the new document, which is processed within 3 business days.

Exchange is free up to 15,000,000 UZS equivalent per month on Standard and unlimited on Plus. If you go over the Standard limit, a 0.6 % fee applies. From Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59, a 0.9 % weekend markup is added because markets are closed.

Chinor uses the interbank mid-market rate during market hours, with a 0.9 % markup at weekends (Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59). You can see the live rate for any of our 14 supported currencies under Exchange in the app before confirming.

Chinor uses the interbank mid-market rate during market hours, with a 0.9 % markup at weekends (Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59). You can see the live rate for any of our 14 supported currencies under Exchange in the app before confirming.
You can exchange more than 14 currencies, including UZS, USD, EUR, and others. To see the full list, go to Exchange in the app.

Yes, the app can exchange currencies. Open Exchange, choose the currency pair and amount, and confirm — the balance is converted instantly at the interbank mid-market rate. You can hold up to 14 currencies, and exchanges are free up to 15,000,000 UZS per month on Standard.

Every fee appears as a separate line under the transaction in the app. Possible fees include the 0.9 % weekend markup and the 1.3 % fee above the free ATM allowance. If the fee doesn’t match these, a human agent can review it.

Every fee appears as a separate line under the transaction in the app. The possible fees are the 0.9 % weekend markup, the 0.6 % fee above the exchange allowance, the 0.5 % fee at gambling or money-transfer merchants, the 1.3 % fee above the free ATM allowance, the 1.1 % credit-card top-up fee, and the 25,000 UZS Plus subscription. If the fee line does not match any of these, a human agent can review it.

A failed transfer is returned to your balance within 2 business days, and the app shows the reason — most often wrong recipient details, a limit, sanctions screening or insufficient balance. Correct the details and send it again; if it fails again for no shown reason, a human agent can check it.
You can hold balances in 14 currencies: UZS, USD, EUR, GBP, RUB, KZT, KGS, TRY, AED, JPY, CNY, CHF, PLN and GEL. You exchange between them in the app under Exchange.
Go to Cards → New virtual card in the app and choose Disposable. You can create up to 6 per day, with a maximum of 3,000,000 UZS per payment. The details regenerate after each use.

You can save your card for use in the app under Cards → Add card. The card must be a Visa, Mastercard, UzCard or Humo card in your own name. Debit-card top-ups are free; credit-card top-ups carry a 1.1 % fee.

Order a physical card in the app under Cards → Order card. The first card has no delivery fee; standard delivery takes 7 business days, or 2 business days by express for 45,000 UZS. Standard customers can hold 1 physical card and Plus customers 2.

A spare (second) physical card is included in the Chinor Plus plan. On Standard, an additional physical card beyond the plan allowance costs 35,000 UZS. You can order it under Cards → Order card; delivery takes 7 business days.

Yes, you can create a virtual card instantly in the app under Cards → New virtual card. Standard customers can have 1 virtual card at a time, and Plus customers can have up to 5. Virtual cards work online and in Apple Pay and Google Pay.

Freeze your card immediately in the app under Cards → Freeze, on the web portal, or by calling the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22. The first replacement each calendar year is free. Dispute any transaction you do not recognise within 60 days.
Log in on the Chinor web portal to freeze all your cards and sign out all devices. If you cannot access the portal, call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22.
Log in on the Chinor web portal to freeze all your cards and sign out all devices. If you cannot access the portal, call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22.

You can order a physical card in the app under Cards → Order card and choose Visa (default) or Mastercard. Standard delivery takes 7 business days, and express delivery takes 2 business days for 45,000 UZS.

Tap Forgot passcode on the app login screen. You will record a new selfie video, which is matched against your verified identity document, and then set a new 6-digit passcode; the reset takes effect immediately. I cannot reset or see your passcode.

A card payment can stay pending for up to 9 business days until the merchant settles it; a pre-authorisation that is never settled (hotels, fuel pumps, car rental) is released automatically after the same 9 business days. The amount is reserved from your balance in the meantime.

A pending ATM withdrawal settles within 4 business days; the amount is already reserved, so you will not be charged twice when it settles. If it is still pending after that, a human agent can check it.

Card top-ups are normally instant but can take up to 2 business days when the card issuer holds them; bank-transfer top-ups are credited within 1 business day. If the time has passed, ask your card issuer or bank whether the payment left, and a human agent can trace it with the reference.

After 3 wrong attempts, the PIN is blocked. You can unblock it in the app under Cards → Security → Unblock PIN. The unblock takes effect at your next chip transaction at any ATM or terminal.

For a domestic transfer, the sender needs your 20-digit Chinor account number and the bank code 00099. For an international transfer, they need your account number, the bank name (Chinor Bank, Tashkent), and the BIC CHNRUZTA. You can find these details in the app under Account → Details.

For a domestic transfer, the sender needs your 20-digit Chinor account number and the bank code 00099. For an international transfer, they need your account number, the bank name (Chinor Bank, Tashkent), and the BIC CHNRUZTA. You can find these details in the app under Account → Details.

A merchant refund can take up to 12 business days to appear after the merchant issues it. Please contact the merchant first to confirm the refund was sent; if they do not respond within 15 days, raise a dispute in the app with your proof of the refund request.

A reverted card payment is usually a pre-authorisation — for example at a hotel, fuel pump or car rental — that the merchant did not settle, so the reserved amount was released back to your balance. Pre-authorisations are released automatically after 9 business days at the latest.

You can request to close your account in the app under Profile → Close account. Your balance must be zero with no pending transactions or open disputes. The closure process is completed within 14 days.
Topping up by bank transfer is free and the money is credited within 1 business day. Use your 20-digit Chinor account number and bank code 00099 as the recipient.

Top-ups from a debit card are free. If you use a credit card, there is a 1.1 % fee, which will be shown before you confirm the transaction. The card must be a Visa, Mastercard, UzCard or Humo card in your own name.

You can top up with cash free of charge at any Chinor ATM, where the amount will be credited immediately. Branch counter deposits are also accepted and credited by the end of the same business day. Chinor does not accept cheques.

A top-up may be denied if the card issuer declined it, the card is not in your own name, the 30,000,000 UZS daily or 100,000,000 UZS monthly top-up limit was reached, or 3-D Secure was not completed. You can check the reason under the attempt in the app; if the money left your card, it will be returned within 5 business days.

Top-up limits are 30,000,000 UZS per day and 100,000,000 UZS per month. If a single deposit exceeds 10,000,000 UZS or your total deposits in a month are over 50,000,000 UZS, you may need to upload proof of the source of funds in the app within 10 days.

A reverted top-up happens when the card issuer declines the payment after an initial authorisation. The amount is returned to your source card within 5 business days; you can then try again or use a bank transfer, which is free and credited within 1 business day.

Go to Account → Top up in the app, add a Visa, Mastercard, UzCard or Humo card in your own name, and enter the amount. Debit-card top-ups are free and normally instant; credit-card top-ups carry a 1.1 % fee. Limits are 30,000,000 UZS per day and 100,000,000 UZS per month.

Go to Account → Top up in the app, add a Visa, Mastercard, UzCard or Humo card in your own name, and enter the amount. Debit-card top-ups are free and normally instant; credit-card top-ups carry a 1.1 % fee. Limits are 30,000,000 UZS per day and 100,000,000 UZS per month.

Domestic transfers are free for the first 20 per month; the 21st and any subsequent transfers cost 2,500 UZS each. International transfers have a 0.8 % fee. The fee is shown as a separate line under the transfer.
To receive money from another bank, provide the sender with your 20-digit Chinor account number and the bank code 00099. Domestic payments sent before 16:30 arrive the same business day.

Yes, you can add funds to your card directly from your bank account using the app. Go to Account → Top up, add a Visa, Mastercard, UzCard or Humo card in your own name, and enter the amount. Debit-card top-ups are free and normally instant; credit-card top-ups carry a 1.1 % fee. The daily limit is 30,000,000 UZS.

Transfers between Chinor accounts are instant. Transfers to other Uzbek banks arrive the same business day if sent before 16:30, otherwise the next business day. International (SWIFT) transfers take 2–4 business days.

If the transfer shows Sent and the normal time has passed — same business day for domestic transfers sent before 16:30, 2–4 business days for international ones — a human agent can trace it. Please have the 16-character reference starting with CB from the transfer screen ready and open in-app chat (daily 08:00–22:00).

Funds from transfers between Chinor accounts are instant. For transfers to other Uzbek banks, funds arrive the same business day if sent before 16:30, otherwise the next business day. International (SWIFT) transfers take 2–4 business days.

In the app, upload your passport or national ID and record a short selfie video. Verification is usually completed within 2 hours and at most 1 business day; you will be notified in the app when it is done.

Chinor may ask for proof of the source of funds if your deposits exceed 50,000,000 UZS in a calendar month or a single top-up is over 10,000,000 UZS. You’ll need to upload documents like a salary slip, sale contract, or tax statement in the app within 10 days. The amount concerned will be held until then, but the rest of your account remains available.

By anti-money-laundering law, Chinor may ask for proof of the source of funds — a salary slip, sale contract or tax statement — when deposits exceed 50,000,000 UZS in a calendar month or a single top-up exceeds 10,000,000 UZS. Upload the documents in the app within 10 days; the amount concerned is held meanwhile, but the rest of your account works normally.

If your top-up is above 10,000,000 UZS, it may be held until you upload proof of the source of funds in the app within 10 days. Smaller top-ups are not held unless your monthly deposits exceed 50,000,000 UZS.

Check that your virtual card is not frozen and that online payments are enabled under Cards → Security. Make sure to complete the 3-D Secure prompt in the app when required by the merchant. Note that a disposable card can only be used for a single payment of up to 3,000,000 UZS and is not suitable for subscriptions.

Check that the virtual card is not frozen and that online payments are switched on under Cards → Security, and complete the 3-D Secure prompt in the app when the merchant asks for it. A disposable card works for a single payment of up to 3,000,000 UZS and cannot be used for subscriptions.

Identity verification is required by anti-money-laundering law before an account can be used; it also protects your account from being opened or used by someone else. It takes a passport or national ID card and a selfie video, and is usually completed within 2 hours.

If the ATM did not dispense the full amount you requested, report the issue from the transaction in the app within 48 hours. The ATM operator's cash reconciliation takes up to 14 business days, and the difference is credited to your balance when it is confirmed.
